chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Abu al-Hasan al-Mazi (peace be upon him), who said:
He is not from us, the one who does not account for himself every day. So if he does good, he asks Allah for increase, and if he does evil, he seeks forgiveness from Allah for it and repents to Him.
ai.seo_question: What is the daily practice that distinguishes a true follower of the Ahl al-Bayt according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Shia concept of *muhasabah* (self-accounting) as a daily spiritual discipline, distinguishing the true adherent through proactive gratitude for good deeds and immediate repentance for sins. It reflects the scholarly emphasis on continuous self-reflection as a means to maintain spiritual equilibrium and closeness to God, rooted in the teachings of the Imams.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Ibrahim Bin Umar Al Yamani, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Maazy<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said:

‘He is not from us<sup>asws</sup>, the one who does not account himself during every day. So if he has done good deeds, he would ask Allah<sup>azwj</sup> for an increase, and if he has done evil deeds, he would seek Forgiveness of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> from it and repent to Him<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Ibrahim ibn ‘Umar al-Yamani from abu al-Hassan (Ali ibn al-Husayn) (a.s.) who has said the following: “

One who does not evaluate his deeds every day is not one of us. One must evaluate his deeds and pray to Allah to increase his good deeds, plead for forgiveness to Allah due to one’s committing evil deeds and turn to Him in repentance.”
